title: phase-anchored-canary-timeline-and-acceptance-signatures-for-eval-driven-rollouts
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Create a phase-anchored canary timeline and an associated set of acceptance signatures (observable checks + qualitative evals) for rolling out model and runtime changes. This ticket scopes the runbook, success criteria, signal thresholds, and cross-team playbooks required to graduate an experiment from 0% to 100% traffic under constraints of latency SLOs and output quality baselines.
hypothesis: Anchoring canary phases to explicit observability signatures (latency percentiles, token cost delta, and prompt-level quality regressions) will reduce undetected regressions during rollouts and enable automated, auditable gates for safe traffic growth without significantly increasing time-to-scale.
success_metrics: No sev-level incidents caused by experiment within 30 days of rollout
Median generation latency within 5% of pre-rollout baseline during staged traffic
False positive rollback rate under 3% for evaluated experiments
Detected quality regressions covered by automated prompts >= 85%
acceptance_criteria: Defined phase boundaries: canary (1%), ramp (5%, 25%), validation (50%), full (100%) with duration windows
For each phase, metric signatures defined: latency p50/p95, error rate, token cost delta, embedding drift, and prompt-slot evaluation pass rate
Automated checks implemented in telemetry to compute signatures and emit pass/fail at phase end
Runbook for manual inspection and escalation linked and validated by SRE, ML Infra, and Product
Canary configuration templatized in console and infra-as-code for quick reuse
milestones: 2026-03-09: Draft signature matrix and initial phase durations produced
2026-03-12: Cross-functional review with SRE/ML/UX completed; feedback captured
2026-03-19: Telemetry queries and dashboard panels wired for signature collection
2026-03-24: Automation to compute phase pass/fail and trigger gates implemented
2026-03-28: Internal dry-run with low-risk change and postmortem capture
2026-04-02: Finalize runbook, publish docs, and mark ticket Done
rollout_plan: 1) Reserve a canary window and select a low-traffic cohort. 2) Deploy change behind a feature toggle to canary cohort (1%). 3) Run automated signature collection for the configured window (24-72h). 4) If signatures pass, incrementally increase traffic per phase durations. 5) At each phase boundary, run prompt-level quality evals against golden prompt set; combine automated and manual signals before advancing. 6) If any hard rollback trigger fires, execute immediate fallback to pinned model version and open incident channel.
monitoring_playbook: Dashboards: canary-signature-board (latency, errors, cost, eval pass rate). Alerts: phase-failure (urgent), slow-degradation (P1), cost-delta-above-threshold (P2). Query templates and saved dashboards are linked below. Paging: SRE on-call + ML infra owner + PM. Post-phase checklist includes data snapshot, sample generations for triage, and PR reference to the model/config change.
rollback_triggers: Latency p95 increase > 20% sustained over phase window
Token cost delta > 15% without corresponding quality improvement
Prompt-eval failure rate > 5% absolute or > 2 standard deviations above baseline
High-severity customer complaints correlated to changes
notes: 2026-03-06: Decided to include both automated eval pass rate and a short manual QA sign-off for validation phase after PM/Design feedback
2026-03-10: SRE requested a default max phase duration of 72h to avoid prolonged exposure; ML infra suggested 24h min windows for small traffic increments
